title: Integer Sizes
concept: XIOM offers integers of different bit sizes — from tiny Int8 to huge Int64 — for memory efficiency.
why: Not every number needs 64 bits. Choosing smaller types saves memory and communicates intent about your data.
syntax_ref:
let x: Int8 = 100;    // 8-bit signed integer
let x: Int16 = 30000;  // 16-bit signed integer
let x: Int32 = 2_000_000_000; // 32-bit
let x: Int64 = huge;   // 64-bit
let x: Int = 42;       // 64-bit (default)
tips: `Int` is 64-bit — it's the default and works for almost everything
Smaller types save memory when you have millions of values
`Int8` ranges from -128 to 127 — perfect for age or day of month
Only use smaller types when you have a specific reason
common_mistakes: Trying to store 1000 in an Int8 — it only goes up to 127!
Using Int8 or Int16 unnecessarily — `Int` is the right default
Confusing bit sizes with decimal digits — 8 bits doesn't mean 8 digits
